title: The fullest monsoon ever
units_note: All money figures in ₹ lakh unless marked. Costs are shown in brackets, e.g. (95.0). Figures compare July to September this year with the same quarter last year.

brief.headline: Occupancy up from 52% to 71%. Profit down 25%.
brief.story: Neelgiri Stays runs three hill hotels in Ooty with 120 rooms between them. The monsoon quarter is usually its slowest, but this year the hotels were busier than ever and revenue rose 12%. Yet EBITDA fell from ₹85L to ₹64L. The general manager says it's OTA commissions and a competitor's price war. The owners want the real answer before the December peak season.

causes.label: OTA commissions went up
causes.feedback: The rate stayed at 18% and commissions were ₹31.6L and ₹31.5L.

causes.label: A competitor's price war forced room rates down
causes.feedback: Leisure ADR went up, from ₹5,100 to ₹5,200. The overall ADR falls only because the cheap corporate rooms are mixed in.

causes.label: Staff overtime from the higher occupancy
The corporate all-inclusive contract is priced below what each room-night costs to serve
Food prices and kitchen waste in the restaurants
causes.feedback: Leisure food costs held at 35% of F&B revenue, and cost per cover matches the menu. The jump in food costs is the corporate meals.

causes.label: Fewer leisure guests
causes.feedback: Leisure room-nights dipped 2%, and leisure revenue was flat.

causes.label: More rooms in use means higher cost per room
causes.feedback: Cost per occupied room-night was ₹1,100 in both years. Volume isn't the problem; the price paid for some of that volume is.

causes.label: Noisy corporate groups drove away leisure guests
causes.feedback: One review complains, but leisure bookings and rates held.

causes.label: The corporate client is paying late
causes.feedback: TechNova pays within 30 days, with every invoice paid.

causes.label: Kitchen staff are stealing food
causes.feedback: Cost per cover matches the menu costing exactly.

causes.label: The corporate room rate is too low compared with leisure rates
causes.feedback: Bulk rates are normally lower than leisure rates. The real problem is that ₹2,200 is below the ₹3,100 it costs to serve that room-night.

bonus.question: The TechNova contract runs to December. If it's renegotiated to ₹3,400 per room-night, all-inclusive, at the same ~2,238 room-nights a quarter, roughly how much does quarterly EBITDA change compared with staying at ₹2,200?
options: No change; costs rise with the rate
bonus.explanation: The costs of serving TechNova don't change with the price, so every extra rupee is profit: ₹1,200 more × 2,238 room-nights ≈ ₹26.9L a quarter. At ₹3,400 each room-night earns ₹300 above its ₹3,100 cost instead of losing ₹900.

explanation.answer: The TechNova contract pays ₹2,200 per room-night for a room plus three meals. Serving that room-night costs ₹1,100 in housekeeping and ₹2,000 in food: ₹3,100. Every one of the 2,238 corporate room-nights lost ₹900, about ₹20.2L in the quarter. That's 94% of the ₹21.5L drop.
fastest_path: Open the P&L. A new package revenue line appeared, and food costs jumped from ₹28L to ₹72.5L.
Open the corporate contract. 2,238 room-nights at ₹2,200, all meals included.
Open kitchen costing. Three meals cost ₹2,000 per guest.
Open housekeeping & room costs. Each occupied room-night costs another ₹1,100. ₹3,100 to serve, ₹2,200 earned.
traps: Occupancy and RevPAR both look fantastic. They're the misleading file: they count the loss-making rooms as success.
The competitor's 10% price cut and OTA commissions are the GM's story, but leisure rates rose and commissions were flat.
"The corporate rate is too low compared with leisure" is the near-miss: a bulk discount is normal, a rate below cost isn't.
explanation.lesson: Filling rooms is only good business if each room earns more than it costs to serve.
